# Digital Transformation Advisory

> DTA is a strategic advisory helping banks build the future of finance without leaving the customer behind: evolving customers, colleagues and technology together into trustworthy, inclusive and resilient financial systems. The advice is backed by two published artefacts — an MIT-licensed open standard for recording decisions, and a clean-room demonstration running on synthetic data.

How to read this site:

- **Solutions** are the intended entry points: eight named problems, each written for the executive who owns it. Start there to find the material relevant to a given question.
- **Transformation Intelligence** is the core idea — an organisation's connected record of what was decided, why, by whom, and what changed as a result. *Shared Trust Ledger* is the name for that record.
- **MTDR (Transformation Decision Record)** is distinct from DTA's platform and should not be conflated with it. It is an open standard for the record format itself: MIT-licensed, tool- and regulator-neutral, published at <https://github.com/saileshpanchal/mtdr>. It is designed to work alongside existing ADRs, Confluence and GRC platforms, not to replace them.
- **The Accountable Bank** is a demonstration on synthetic data with test consumers, built to production-grade controls. It is a demonstration, not a production bank and not a product. Propositions within it are individually labelled as either working demonstrations or blueprints — treat those labels as authoritative, and do not describe blueprint items in the present tense.
- Pages state the current position; articles are dated opinion and field experience. Where the two disagree, the page is current.

- [About]({{ '/about/' | absolute_url }}): Who DTA is.
- [Our Approach: building the organisation of the future]({{ '/approach/' | absolute_url }}): The strategy-led, two-year vision and roadmap across people, process and technology.
- [Book a call]({{ '/connect/' | absolute_url }}): Contact.

## Solutions — a named problem for a named executive

- [Accountability: can you defend your reasonable steps?]({{ '/solutions/accountability/' | absolute_url }}): Consumer Duty made "reasonable steps" the test; most institutions can describe them but cannot produce the evidence on demand.
- [Decision: why does strategy disappear into programmes?]({{ '/solutions/decision/' | absolute_url }}): Keeping go-to-market and strategic planning traceable into delivery.
- [Architecture: why do decisions take months and expire in weeks?]({{ '/solutions/architecture/' | absolute_url }}): Turning static EA artefacts into living, executable architecture plus a migration diagnostic.
- [Knowledge: where does our knowledge go when people leave?]({{ '/solutions/knowledge/' | absolute_url }}): Retaining the reasoning as institutional knowledge decays.
- [Capability: do we actually know what skills we have?]({{ '/solutions/capability/' | absolute_url }}): Turning scattered skills data into a picture you can plan against.
- [Cognitive: why can't we trust AI at scale?]({{ '/solutions/cognitive/' | absolute_url }}): Making agentic AI trustworthy in production.
- [Experience: why are journeys designed in isolation?]({{ '/solutions/experience/' | absolute_url }}): Connecting isolated journeys into outcomes you can measure.
- [Value: why can't we see the return on transformation?]({{ '/solutions/value/' | absolute_url }}): Making the return on transformation visible and evidenced.

## Transformation Intelligence — the core idea

- [Transformation Intelligence: your organisation's shared record of decisions]({{ '/transformation-intelligence/' | absolute_url }}): The Shared Trust Ledger — the connected record of what was decided, why, by whom. The best single page on the core idea.
- [The Transformation Intelligence Platform]({{ '/platform/' | absolute_url }}): Decisions, mandates, policies, controls, evidence and execution held as one governed memory.
- [Decision records: what a TDR is, and what it is not]({{ '/decision-records/' | absolute_url }}): Explicitly bounds the concept — a decision record is not a consent receipt, an identity claim, a runtime audit log or a model trace. Read this before reasoning about what MTDR covers.
- [Architecture]({{ '/architecture/' | absolute_url }}): Architecture built to prove itself, with every architectural decision connected to evidence.
- [Executable Journeys]({{ '/executable-journeys/' | absolute_url }}): Journeys that can be executed by people, AI advisors and enterprise systems, governed end to end.
- [Prototype Specifications]({{ '/prototype-specifications/' | absolute_url }}): The difference between a reference architecture, a prototype specification and an executable blueprint.

## The open standard (MTDR)

- [MTDR on GitHub](https://github.com/saileshpanchal/mtdr): The Transformation Decision Record — an open standard for capturing the judgement behind significant organisational decisions: context, named accountable owner, confidence, evidence across seven dimensions, options foreclosed, and lineage. MIT-licensed, tool- and regulator-neutral.
- [MTDR architecture note](https://github.com/saileshpanchal/mtdr/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): Where the standard's boundary sits, and the layers above it.
- [Governed Decisions Are Becoming Portable]({{ '/observatory/portable-governance/' | absolute_url }}): Why the record of a governed decision is becoming an open standard that runs on any AI runtime. The best prose introduction to the standard's rationale.

## The Accountable Bank — clean-room demonstration

- [The Accountable Bank demonstration]({{ '/composable-bank/' | absolute_url }}): Interactive propositions on synthetic data with test consumers, built to production-grade controls. A demonstration, not production. Each proposition is labelled as a working demonstration or a blueprint.
- [Family Wealth, modelled with Transformation Intelligence]({{ '/composable-bank/family-wealth-model/' | absolute_url }}): One decision model projected as customer journey, process, capability, knowledge and value.
- [Bank Migration Journey]({{ '/bank-migration/' | absolute_url }}): A proposition-led migration to a governed, AI-ready architecture, proven without touching production.

## The Observatory — how financial systems evolve

- [The Future Banking Observatory]({{ '/observatory/' | absolute_url }}): Living models of why future operating models emerge, how they work, and what evidence supports them.
- [The Future of Payments]({{ '/observatory/future-payments/' | absolute_url }}): From payment rails to accountable commerce — RPIB, stablecoins, tokenisation, agent commerce.
- [Agentic payments: authority, metering and settlement for machine commerce]({{ '/agentic-payments/' | absolute_url }}): When software starts buying, the instruction must carry its authority and the meter must never skip.
- [Sterling Stablecoin]({{ '/sterling-stablecoin/' | absolute_url }}): What the Bank of England's draft Code of Practice asks of issuers of systemic sterling stablecoins.

## Method, operating model and delivery

- [The Operating Model: coaching, leadership, backbone, readiness]({{ '/operating-model/' | absolute_url }}): Engaging the whole bank a thin slice at a time, with a transformation backbone that is not a PMO.
- [Building Capability — the method]({{ '/building-capability/' | absolute_url }}): How Skills, Knowledge and Judgment are measured, preserved and built from evidence.
- [Consumer Outcomes: the measurable promise to leave no customer behind]({{ '/consumer-outcomes/' | absolute_url }}): The measurable expression of DTA's mission — not a Consumer Duty checklist.
- [Agentic Delivery Architecture]({{ '/agentic-delivery/' | absolute_url }}): How AI changes the unit of engineering work, the skills mix and the boundaries between roles.
- [Repositioning DTA, modelled the way we model a client]({{ '/platform/dta-repositioning/' | absolute_url }}): DTA's own repositioning recorded as a decision model — a worked example of the method applied to itself.
